plan: Given my private value of $21, I aim to bid slightly below it to maximize potential profit while ensuring I have a chance to win. I anticipate others may bid near their values, so I will bid $19. This is high enough to potentially win if others bid conservatively, but low enough to maintain a profit margin if I win. I avoid bidding my full value to ensure profit if I win and pay the third-highest bid. This strategic balance aims to optimize long-term gain.

Given my value of $22, I aim to win while minimizing payment. I expect others to bid around their values, averaging $24.5. To win, I should bid slightly above this. Bidding $25 increases win probability while ensuring profit if I win, as I pay the third-highest bid. Bidding lower risks losing, while higher reduces profit. This balance maximizes long-term profit potential.

Given my value of $13, I aim to maximize profit by winning only if the third-highest bid is significantly lower. I expect others to bid close to their values. If I bid slightly above half my value, e.g., $7, I might win if others undervalue their bids. This balances the risk of overpaying and the chance of winning with profit. I will bid $7, hoping the third bid is lower, thus securing a profit if I win.
